topic: How to Pick Colors That Don't Look AI-Generated — accent discipline, why indigo/blue defaults scream slop, picking one accent and committing, warm vs cold neutrals
title: Why every AI app is the same shade of blue
caption:
Ever notice how every new AI app ships the same indigo? That's not a coincidence — it's the default.

Bootstrap blue, Tailwind indigo, #6366F1 everywhere. Reaching for blue is the fastest way to look generic.

The fix:
01. Pick ONE accent and commit — use it for actions, not decoration
02. Kill the default indigo/blue
03. Nudge your neutrals warm or cool (pure grey looks cheap)
04. Check your palette in greyscale first

Color is a choice. Make one.

topic: The Spacing Rules That Make UI Look Designed — the 8pt grid, generous section padding, grouping by proximity, why cramped UI reads as amateur
title: Same layout, way more space — that's the whole trick
caption:
Most UI that feels a little 'off' has the same problem: no space.

Good news is you don't have to redesign anything. Usually the fix is just room. Put everything on an 8pt grid so your gaps stop looking random. Give your sections way more padding than feels necessary. Keep related stuff close together, and push the unrelated stuff apart.

Same layout, more breathing room, and suddenly it looks like someone who knew what they were doing built it.

topic: Dark Mode Mistakes That Make Your App Look Cheap — pure black vs warm charcoal, dimming text instead of pure white, desaturating accents on dark, elevation through lightness
title: Your dark mode looks cheap, and it's an easy fix
caption:
Dark mode is more than a black background and white text. That's usually why it ends up looking cheap.

A few quick fixes. Skip pure black — it's harsh and makes every edge buzz. Use a warm charcoal instead, around #1C1A17. Don't use pure white text either; pull it back to a soft cream so it doesn't glare. Take that bright accent from light mode and knock the saturation down so it glows instead of blinding people. And forget shadows — in dark mode, higher surfaces just get lighter.

Do those four things and your dark mode stops looking like a default and starts looking designed.
